name: Enterprise Cloud deployment
description: Default enterprise deployment model. Brain + DevBox both run in Cognition Cloud. Public network or IP-allowlist for customer resource access. Fastest setup (minutes). Works when SCM (GitHub.com / GitLab.com / Azure DevOps Cloud) and artifact stores are public or IP-whitelistable. Does NOT support MFA VPN access to customer resources.

name: Customer Dedicated Deployment
description: Single-tenant Cognition-managed VPC for customers with private networks that cannot support IP allowlisting. Brain stays in Cognition Cloud; DevBox runs in customer-isolated VPC. Connects via AWS PrivateLink (preferred) or IPSec tunnel. Supports MFA VPN access to internal resources and OpenVPN.

name: Devin Brain (Cognition Cloud)
description: Stateless cloud-based service powering Devin's intelligence. ALWAYS resides in Cognition Cloud (similar to GitHub Copilot's architecture). Pairs with the DevBox (which can be in customer-dedicated VPC under that deployment model).

name: AWS PrivateLink (Customer Dedicated networking)
description: Preferred secure-tunnel option between customer VPC and Cognition's single-tenant VPC for Customer Dedicated deployments. Alternative: IPSec tunnel.

name: *.devinapps.com end-user domain
description: Domain serving Devin's interactive session tools (IDE / VSCode frontend, Desktop / browser viewer) loaded via iframes in the user's browser. End-user workstations must be able to reach `*.devinapps.com` over HTTPS/443 — corporate proxies/firewalls must allowlist it.

name: Cross-tenant WebSocket startup
description: On startup, Devin establishes a secure WebSocket connection from the customer DevBox to an isolated container in Cognition's tenant. All subsequent operations occur over this secure channel. Backend session isolation enforced.

name: Compound AI system (no third-party LLM keys)
description: Devin is described in the FAQ as a compound AI system. Does NOT currently support customer-supplied third-party LLM API keys. The Brain owns model selection.

name: Rollout mode — Not enabled
description: Initial state for declarative environment configuration before enterprise activation. No orgs see environment pages; all use classic setup. Activation requires Cognition admin contact.

name: Rollout mode — Testing
description: Baseline rollout state after activation. Only manually opted-in orgs use blueprints. All other orgs remain on classic setup with no UI changes. Enterprise admin opts orgs in from the Rollout page. Used for piloting blueprint configuration in isolation.

name: Rollout mode — Available
description: Self-service rollout state. Org admins on classic setup see a migration callout on their Machine Configuration page and can self-service migrate. No automatic switch — opt-in only. Useful for awareness + paced migration.

name: Rollout mode — Enabled by default
description: Final rollout state. New orgs default to declarative blueprints. Existing orgs that were on classic with repos receive automatic classic overrides as a safety mechanism. PERMANENT action — cannot be undone without a Cognition administrator.

name: Per-org rollout override
description: Enterprise admin can opt individual orgs in (Testing/Available mode) or out (Enabled by default mode) from the Rollout page's per-org table. Switches an org between blueprints and classic setup. Both blueprint and classic configs are preserved during switches.

name: Automatic classic override
description: Safety mechanism activated when switching to Enabled-by-default mode. Any org currently on classic setup AND with repositories configured automatically receives an explicit classic override — nothing changes for them. Orgs without repos (or already on blueprints) are unaffected.

name: Migration assistant (classic → declarative)
description: Devin-driven assistant that inspects an org's existing snapshot and generates equivalent blueprint configuration. Lowers the per-org migration burden. Documented at /onboard-devin/environment/migration.

name: Rollout KPI dashboard
description: Top-of-Rollout-page summary metrics: Blueprint orgs (count), Rollout percentage (% on blueprints), Build health (aggregate status across blueprint orgs).

name: Per-org rollout table
description: Detailed table on the Rollout page showing every org with: Organization, State (Blueprints|Classic), Override (yes/no), Classic repos (count), Blueprint repos (count), Latest build status. Filterable by All / Blueprints / Classic / Overrides.

name: Three-tier blueprint hierarchy (additive)
description: Enterprise → Organization → Repository. Additive (lower tiers don't replace upper). Enterprise blueprint runs first (baseline), then org, then repo. Knowledge items from all tiers are collected; multiple tiers can define same-named knowledge item without overwriting.

name: Enterprise blueprint
description: Enterprise-tier blueprint at Settings > Devin's base environment. Default home for: standard language runtimes, security tools, corporate certificates, internal CLIs, proxy settings, registry auth. Recommended pattern: put it here unless a specific reason to scope narrower.

name: Enterprise secret
description: Secret defined at the enterprise tier. Available in EVERY build and EVERY session across ALL organizations, in enterprise/org/repo blueprint steps alike. Managed in Settings > Devin's base environment > Secrets. Requires ManageAccountResources permission.

name: Enterprise-wide rebuild
description: Cascading rebuild from the enterprise tier across ALL organizations. Triggered by enterprise-blueprint update, secret rotation, or post-security-patch refresh. Each org's build runs with updated enterprise blueprint + own org/repo blueprints. Respects per-org build queue (queues behind in-progress; cancels-and-replaces queued).

name: Cascading secret precedence
description: Secrets cascade through enterprise → org → repo with more specific tiers winning on name collision. Use to override enterprise-wide credentials with team-specific tokens that have different permissions.

name: Organization-level role (RBAC)
description: Org-by-org assigned RBAC role. Built-in roles: Admin (full org access), Member (standard), DeepWiki Only (DeepWiki + AskDevin + index repos only). Assignment via Org Settings > Organization Members. Custom org roles created from Enterprise Settings > Roles by users with Manage Account Membership permission.

name: Account-level (enterprise) role (RBAC)
description: Enterprise-wide role applying across all organizations. Users with account-level roles automatically inherit corresponding org-level permissions in every org they belong to. Built-in: Admin, Member.

name: IdP group → role auto-assignment
description: Enterprise feature mapping IdP groups to Devin roles. When users authenticate via SSO, they automatically receive the role assigned to their IdP group. Configured in Enterprise Settings > Members. Requires SSO provider to send the `groups` array in the SSO assertion.

name: SSO via Okta (OpenID Connect)
description: Enterprise SSO option configured against an Okta tenant via OIDC.

name: SSO via Azure AD
description: Enterprise SSO option for Azure AD / Entra ID.

name: SSO via generic SAML 2.0
description: Enterprise SSO option for any generic SAML 2.0 identity provider.

name: SSO via generic OIDC
description: Enterprise SSO option for any generic OpenID Connect provider.

name: Trust Center (trust.cognition.ai)
description: Public security-posture surface at https://trust.cognition.ai. Documents SOC 2 Type II findings, security policies, and certifications.

name: SOC 2 Type II (September 2024)
description: Cognition's SOC 2 Type II certification obtained in September 2024 (the enterprise-overview cites this date; the admin-security page cites March 2024 — likely Type I → Type II progression). Covers data security, privacy, processing integrity, confidentiality, availability.

name: Dedicated/on-prem data residency
description: For Enterprise customers using dedicated or on-prem deployments, ALL customer data is stored within the customer's own tenant. Cognition does not train on this data regardless of opt-in.

name: Weekly build-health review cadence
description: Recommended best-practice cadence: check build health weekly across all orgs. Look for: Failed builds (critical, blocks all repos), Partial builds (some repos failing — usually dependency/blueprint drift), Stale builds (unusually old latest-build — possibly stuck queue).

name: Blueprint template library
description: Curated copy-paste blueprint templates for Python, Node.js, Go, Java, Ruby, Rust, advanced patterns. Located at /onboard-devin/environment/templates. Used internally by enterprise admins to share standard configs across teams.

name: Audit-logged rollout transitions
description: All rollout state transitions are recorded in audit logs. Captures: enterprise mode changes (Testing → Available, Enabled-by-default activation), per-org override changes (opt-in / opt-out / removal), the admin who made each change, and timestamp.

name: Concurrency-protected state transitions
description: If another admin changes enterprise rollout state between page-load and submit, the request is rejected with a conflict error. Prevents accidental overwrites in multi-admin environments.
